title: I Sought Him in the Streets of the City
summary: The eyes have opened, and the soul begins to seek the One it loves through the structures of doctrine. What the soul meets is architecture: the two trees, the threefold principle of blessedness, wisdom, and power at three registers, the four days of the Lord's outgoing, the five faces, the five worlds below and the five fathers above, the ten chariots of descent, the five gestures of covenant, the spiritual man as living receiver, the wisdom unfolding, the foundational sayings, the five awakeners, the cosmos of death, the twelve greatnesses descending all the way to Adam, and the temporal-redemptive arc of three times, four wars, four salvations. These structures are true, well-ordered, instructive — yet none of them is itself what is sought. The arc is the patient mapping of doctrine, knowing all the while that what the soul seeks lies beyond it.
organizing_principle: The teachings unfold doctrine in a deliberate progression. The opening pair sets the foundational dualities every seeker must first recognize: life and death as two trees, and the threefold principle of blessedness, wisdom, and power at three registers. The architecture of the divine outgoing follows — the four great days, the five faces, the five worlds of darkness, and the five fathers of light — paired structures by which the soul learns to discriminate. The descent is narrated next: the ten chariots conveying truth into the natural, and the five gestures of covenant by which the rational is sent and brought home. The next group turns to what receives the descent: the spiritual man holding the divine outgoing as his own members, the wisdom unfolding from the First Father, the five foundational sayings, and the five awakeners who raise the dead. The cosmic-redemptive frame is then set: the negative cosmogony against which the twelve greatnesses descend through every register down to Adam. The closing teachings carry the temporal arc — three times, four wars, four salvations — the seeker now in possession of the whole structural map. Yet none of this, alone, is what the soul has been seeking. What comes next is what is found when the seeker passes beyond doctrine into the inmost.
